questions.question: What is a stochastic process?
options: A collection $\{X_t\colon t\in T\}$ of random variables.
A single random variable observed at one time $t$.
A probability distribution on the index set $T$.
A collection $\{x_t\colon t\in T\}$ of fixed real numbers.

questions.question: What does the index set $T$ do in a stochastic process?
options: It is the set of values each $X_t$ can take
It is the sample space on which each $X_t$ is defined
It must be a finite set of observation times
It labels the random variables in the family

questions.question: What kind of randomness does a stochastic process describe?
options: Randomness evolving over an index such as time
Only one fixed random value with no index
Only deterministic functions
Only unordered samples drawn without replacement

questions.question: Can the index set of a stochastic process be continuous?
options: No, it must always be finite
No, it must always be the integers
Only if all variables are deterministic
Yes, it may be discrete or continuous

questions.question: What is a sample path?
options: The distribution of $X_t$ at one fixed index $t$
One realization of the process across the index set
The set of all possible realizations of the process
The average of many realizations at each index $t$

questions.question: Daily demand over a year is what type of stochastic process?
options: A discrete-time stochastic process
A continuous-time stochastic process only
A degenerate distribution only
A single event indicator

questions.question: The number of arrivals up to time $t$ in a queue is what kind of process?
options: A discrete-time stochastic process
A single random variable with integer values
A continuous-time stochastic process
A deterministic counting function of $t$

questions.question: Stock prices observed over time form what?
options: A single constant random variable
A combination count
A fixed sample space with no random variables
A stochastic process

questions.question: If $T=\{1,2,3\}$, how many indexed random variables are listed in $\{X_t\colon t\in T\}$?
options: Infinitely many necessarily

questions.question: Which object is a sample path for a daily demand process?
options: One realized sequence of daily demands
Many realized demands for one fixed day
The expected demand on each day of the year
The single largest demand over the year

questions.question: Why must the random variables be on a common probability space?
options: So every $X_t$ has the same marginal distribution.
So the variables $X_t$ are independent of each other.
So all the $X_t$ take values in one common set.
So joint behavior across indices is meaningful.

questions.question: How is a stochastic process different from a single random variable?
options: An indexed family of random variables.
A random variable with a mean that changes in time.
A random variable that can take infinitely many values.
A single random time at which an event occurs.

questions.question: What distinguishes discrete-time from continuous-time processes?
options: The values must be integer or real respectively
The probabilities must be zero or one
The variables must be independent only in discrete time
The type of index set used

questions.question: If $X_t$ is temperature at hour $t$ for $t=0,1,\ldots,24$, what is the index set?
options: All real numbers only
The set of temperatures
The probability space only

questions.question: Which is more naturally a stochastic process than a single random variable?
options: Monthly sales over several years.
The result of one coin toss only.
The value $5$
The event that a die shows six

questions.question: For a queue process $N_t$, what might $N_5$ represent?
options: The fifth possible sample space
The random number of arrivals up to time $5$
The probability that arrivals are impossible
The sample variance of all queues

questions.question: Why is a sample path not the same thing as the process distribution?
options: One realized path vs the law over all paths.
One fixed index $t$ vs all indices in $T$.
The expected path vs one realized path.
Observed past values vs predicted future values.

questions.question: What misconception is avoided by calling a process a family of random variables?
options: Thinking it is a single observed variable.
Thinking its variables can depend on one another.
Thinking its index set may be continuous.
Thinking its values at different times are random.

questions.question: If a process is observed at every real time $t\ge0$, what type of index set is being used?
options: A finite index set of size one
A set of outcomes only
A set of probabilities only
A continuous index set

questions.question: A model lists $X_1,\ldots,X_{365}$ for daily demand. What is one sample path?
options: One year's realized sequence of 365 demands
The average demand only
The event that all the daily demands are positive
The distribution of day 365 alone
